findings.source_passage: Beneath the unclouded and mild azure sky, upon the fair face of the pleasant sea, wafted by the joyous breezes, that great mass of death floats on
findings.why_it_matters: The accumulation of 'unclouded,' 'fair face of the pleasant sea,' and 'joyous breezes' is Melville's deliberate ironic counterpoint to 'that great mass of death'—its compression strips the tonal irony that makes the closing image of the paragraph interpretively central.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'unclouded,' 'upon the fair face of the pleasant sea,' and 'wafted by the joyous breezes' in full; the ironic contrast is load-bearing and the phrase is short enough to retain without budget strain.

findings.source_passage: straightway the whale's unharming corpse, with trembling fingers is set down in the log—_shoals, rocks, and breakers hereabouts: beware!_
findings.why_it_matters: Melville italicizes the log inscription to mark it as a quoted document embedded in narration—a textually distinctive move that signals the transition from description to satirical critique of institutional record-keeping; plain text erases that rhetorical signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore italics on 'shoals, rocks, and breakers hereabouts: beware!' to preserve the typographical voice marker.

summary: Two medium-severity issues: the ironic 'joyous breezes'/'fair face' counterpoint is compressed away, and the italicized log entry loses its typographic distinctiveness; no high-severity signature losses found.
